name: MathlibAnnex.Sphere.finiteDimensional_codomain
title: Finite-dimensionality transfers across a sphere isometry

content.display_title: Finite-dimensionality transfers across a sphere isometry
content.one_sentence_role: Uses the radial homeomorphism to transfer local compactness, then applies the finite-dimensionality criterion for real normed spaces.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $X,Y$ be real normed spaces. Put $S_X=\{x\in X:\|x\|_X=1\}$ and $S_Y=\{y\in Y:\|y\|_Y=1\}$, each with its ambient chord distance. Let $\Delta:S_X\to S_Y$ be a bijective isometry of their unit spheres with the ambient chord metrics. If $X$ is finite-dimensional over $\mathbb R$, then $Y$ is finite-dimensional over $\mathbb R$.
content.assumptions: Only $X$ is assumed finite-dimensional at the start. Both spaces have real normed-vector-space structures, and $\Delta$ is a sphere isometry equivalence. There is no initial completeness or finite-dimensionality assumption on $Y$; the zero-dimensional case is included. The two carriers may have different universes in the formal statement.
content.conclusion: The codomain $Y$ is finite-dimensional. Applying the theorem to $\Delta^{-1}$ transfers finite-dimensionality in the opposite direction; that is the separately cited domain theorem.
content.proof_summary:
For clarity, the radial map is $R_\Delta(0)=0$ and $R_\Delta(x)=\|x\|_X\Delta(x/\|x\|_X)$ for $x\ne0$, with inverse $R_{\Delta^{-1}}$. Use the homeomorphism $R_\Delta:X\to Y$, whose continuity and inverse continuity follow from the two $3$-Lipschitz estimates. Finite-dimensional real normed spaces are proper, so every closed bounded ball in $X$ is compact. Each point therefore has a compact neighbourhood, making $X$ locally compact. A homeomorphism carries a compact neighbourhood to a compact neighbourhood, so $Y$ is locally compact. The local-compactness criterion for a real normed space now implies that $Y$ is finite-dimensional:

$$\begin{gathered}
\dim_{\mathbb R}X<\infty\ \Longrightarrow\ X\text{ locally compact}\\
\Longrightarrow Y\text{ locally compact}\ \Longrightarrow\ \dim_{\mathbb R}Y<\infty.
\end{gathered}$$

proof_steps.text: Finite-dimensionality of $X$ supplies its proper-space structure. This is where the dimension hypothesis is used.

Transfer local compactness through $R_\Delta$. The criterion is then applied to the real normed space $Y$, with the newly obtained local compactness; it requires no separately assumed completeness of $Y$.

content.lean_realization_notes: The map used to carry the topology is the radial homeomorphism $R_\Delta$, with inverse $R_{\Delta^{-1}}$. This step asserts transfer of finite-dimensionality; a linear isometry is not constructed here.
